_note: Phase 3 of docs/premium-skincare-brief.md — [PREMIUM-SKIN]. Demand-side claims from documents actually fetched on 2026-08-10 (two Nykaa investor presentations and one MOFSL initiation note, both read as PDFs; two aggregator pages and one trade-press page read as HTML). Review-language statistics are NOT here — they are computed by lib/transforms/premium_skin_demand.py and ledgered from there. Google Trends indices are NOT here: a normalised relative index has no defensible unit or value_basis, matching lib/fetchers/trends_google.to_data_points.

claims.source_name: Nykaa (FSN E-Commerce Ventures) Q3FY26 investor presentation, Key Performance Metrics
claims.notes: [PREMIUM-SKIN] AVERAGE ORDER VALUE, not a product price: Nykaa Beauty AOV Rs2,173 for the quarter ended 31-Dec-2025 (Rs2,127 in Q3FY25, +2% YoY), company-defined as GMV across websites, apps and physical stores divided by orders. ORGANISED retail, omnichannel (online + Nykaa's own stores). Transaction value after discount, NOT MRP. Reference point for the Rs1,500-3,000 band: one in-band SKU is approximately one whole average beauty order. Basket spans all BPC categories including mass.

claims.source_name: Future Market Insights — K-Beauty Product Market (India country table)
claims.notes: [CORRIDOR][PREMIUM-SKIN] India K-beauty forecast CAGR 7.4% (2026-36) — recorded as an OUTLIER TO DISCARD, not as a candidate base case. Filed at total_bpc because K-beauty spans BPC, not skincare alone, and to sit beside the four K-beauty-in-India estimates the repo already holds: TheBK/Beauty Kyungjae USD400m 2024 growing 25.9% to USD1.6bn by 2030 (MEDIUM), Economic Times Retail 25.9% 2024-30 (MEDIUM), Expert Market Research INR3,139cr 2025 at 26.3% 2026-35 (LOW), The Report Cubes USD335m 2026 at 19.17% (LOW). Those four cluster on LEVEL (~USD326-400m) and on GROWTH (19-26%); FMI's 7.4% is roughly a third of the bottom of that range. Its disclosed method explains why — a 'proprietary forecasting model based on Korean cosmetics export data (KITA), global Sephora K-beauty shelf space allocation, and social commerce GMV tracking', i.e. a global shelf-space model apportioned to a country rather than an India measurement. Channel and organised/unorganised coverage not stated.

claims.source_name: bpc-intel derived (MOFSL income-cohort spend x in-band MRP)
claims.methodology: AFFORDABILITY RATIO, [ESTIMATE] derived from two ledgered figures, not measured. Numerator: an in-band shelf price (MRP). Denominator: MOFSL/Company annual BPC spend per consumer for the highest income cohort (>USD15k p.a.), USD140, converted at the pinned USD/INR 96.23 (config/exchange_rates.yaml, 2026-07-21) = Rs13,472. BASIS MISMATCH stated deliberately: the denominator is annual outlay across ALL BPC categories and ALL channels (organised + unorganised), the numerator is one skincare SKU's MRP in the online channel, so the ratio overstates nothing about margin and is only an affordability index. SENSITIVITY: at Rs1,500 / Rs1,900 / Rs2,900 MRP the ratio is 11.1% / 14.1% / 21.5% against the USD140 cohort, and 13.4% / 17.0% / 26.0% against the mid-level-professional cohort (USD116 = Rs11,163). Purchase frequency for these cohorts is 17-18 occasions a year (MOFSL Exhibit 14), implying ~Rs748 average spend per occasion for the top cohort — an in-band SKU at Rs1,900 is ~2.5x that.
claims.notes: [PREMIUM-SKIN] ONE in-band SKU at Rs1,900 MRP absorbs ~14.1% of the ENTIRE annual BPC budget of India's highest-income consumer cohort (>USD15k p.a., USD140/yr). Rs1,900 is the list price Phase 1 recommends as the floor for holding the band after discounting. Read as the trial constraint on this band: the purchase is a budget event, not a top-up.

claims.source_name: bpc-intel derived (MOFSL income-cohort spend x in-band MRP)
claims.methodology: AFFORDABILITY RATIO, [ESTIMATE] derived from two ledgered figures, not measured. Numerator: an in-band shelf price (MRP). Denominator: MOFSL/Company annual BPC spend per consumer for the highest income cohort (>USD15k p.a.), USD140, converted at the pinned USD/INR 96.23 (config/exchange_rates.yaml, 2026-07-21) = Rs13,472. BASIS MISMATCH stated deliberately: the denominator is annual outlay across ALL BPC categories and ALL channels (organised + unorganised), the numerator is one skincare SKU's MRP in the online channel, so the ratio overstates nothing about margin and is only an affordability index. SENSITIVITY: at Rs1,500 / Rs1,900 / Rs2,900 MRP the ratio is 11.1% / 14.1% / 21.5% against the USD140 cohort, and 13.4% / 17.0% / 26.0% against the mid-level-professional cohort (USD116 = Rs11,163). Purchase frequency for these cohorts is 17-18 occasions a year (MOFSL Exhibit 14), implying ~Rs748 average spend per occasion for the top cohort — an in-band SKU at Rs1,900 is ~2.5x that. This row multiplies the numerator by 4 for a four-SKU launch set.
claims.notes: [PREMIUM-SKIN] A FOUR-SKU routine at Rs1,900 each (Rs7,600) absorbs ~56.4% of the annual BPC budget of the highest-income cohort (>USD15k p.a.). Bears directly on the brief's range-led framing: range economics hold on the ODM/MOQ side, but the CONSUMER cannot be assumed to buy the routine at once. Sequential single-SKU adoption is the realistic path.
